questions.question: What are the key factors that determine the quality of food? Explain any five. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• What are the key factors determine the quality of food? Explain any five.
  • Ans: The quality of food is determined by various factors that ensure it is safe, nutritious,
  • and acceptable to consumers. Here are five key factors:
  • • Nutritional Value- Presence of essential nutrients such as carbohydrates, proteins,
  • fats, vitamins, and minerals in the right proportions.
  • • Freshness- Fresh food is free from spoilage and degradation. It has a natural flavor,
  • aroma, and texture.
  • • Hygiene and Safety- Food should be free from harmful bacteria, viruses, chemicals,
  • and physical contaminants.
  • • Taste and Appearance- Sensory qualities such as color, flavor, texture, and aroma play
  • a major role in consumer acceptance.

questions.question: Discuss the health hazards caused by chemical contaminants in food? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the health hazards caused by chemical contaminants in food?
  • Ans: Chemical contaminants in food are harmful substances that can enter the food supply
  • during farming, processing, packaging, or storage. These contaminants pose serious health
  • hazards.
  • • Acute Poisoning- High levels of chemicals such as pesticides or cleaning agents can
  • cause immediate symptoms like nausea, vomiting, dizziness, abdominal pain, and
  • even death in extreme cases.
  • • Chronic effect- long term exposure to low level of chemicals can lead to serious
  • health problems like cancer, kidney damage and neurological disorders.
  • • Organ damage- Exposure to certain chemicals can damage specific organs like liver or
  • kidney.
  • • Developmental effects- In children, exposure to chemicals can impacts mental
  • intellectual and physical level.
  • • Reproductive issues- Chemical exposure may lead to reproductive problems and birth
  • defects.

questions.question: How food infection can be defined? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• How food infection can be defined?
  • Ans: Food infection refers to a type of foodborne illness that occurs when a person
  • consumes food or water contaminated with pathogenic microorganisms, such as bacteria,
  • viruses, or parasites.
  • • Cause- The ingestion of live microorganisms such as Salmonella, E. coli.
  • • Mechanism- After consumption, the pathogens colonize the gastrointestinal tract
  • and start reproducing, leading to the release of toxins or causing direct damage to
  • the tissues.
  • • Symptoms- Fever, diarrhoea, abdominal cramps, nausea, and vomiting.
  • • Sources- Contaminated water, undercooked meat, unpasteurized milk, raw
  • vegetables, and unhygienically prepared food.
  • • Prevention- Proper cooking, personal hygiene, safe food handling, and clean water
  • supply.

questions.question: Write a detailed note on how relative humidity and water activity affects the growth of microrganisms. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Write a detailed note on how relative humidity and water activity affects the growth
  • of microorganism?
  • Ans: The growth and survival of microorganisms in food are heavily influenced by moisture-
  • related factors, primarily relative humidity (RH) and water activity (aw).
  • Relative Humidity- Relative Humidity is the amount of moisture present in the air compared
  • to the maximum it can hold at a given temperature, expressed as a percentage.
  • • Impact on Food- RH affects the moisture content of foods during storage. If the RH is
  • too high, dry foods may absorb moisture, tends to microbial growth.
  • • Microbial Growth- Molds and some bacteria can grow on food surfaces when RH is
  • high.
  • • Control Measures- Proper packaging and environmental control help maintain
  • optimal RH and minimize microbial risks.
  • Water Activity- Water activity is a measure of the free or available water in a food product
  • for microbial use.
  • • Different microorganisms have minimum aw requirements for growth.
  • • Lowering aw through drying, freezing, or adding solutes like salt and sugar is a
  • common method to preserve food and prevent microbial spoilage

questions.question: What are the preventive measures to control food borne pathogens? / [CO4] [10x1 = 10]
questions.solution_html:
• What are the preventive measures to control food borne pathogens?
  • Ans: Foodborne pathogens such as Salmonella, E. coli, Listeria, and Norovirus are
  • responsible for millions of food-related illnesses globally. Preventing contamination and
  • controlling these pathogens is essential for ensuring food safety.
  • • Personal Hygiene- Regular handwashing with soap and clean water, especially after
  • using the toilet or handling raw food. Use of clean uniforms, gloves, and hairnets to
  • prevent contamination.
  • • Proper Cooking and Temperature Control- Cook food to the correct internal
  • temperature to kill pathogens.
  • • Safe Storage and Refrigeration- Store perishable items in the refrigerator or freezer.
  • Avoid leaving cooked or perishable food at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
  • • Cross-Contamination Prevention- Use separate cutting boards, utensils, and
  • containers for raw and cooked foods.
